author: David Miller, CPA (Corporate Controller)
post_title: Why unapplied cash persists at mid-market B2B companies
full_body_excerpt: At $30M-$80M ARR, remittance advice comes in via every conceivable channel: lockbox checks, EDI 820, bank email attachments, customer vendor portals. ERP auto-reconciliation breaks down, leaving hundreds of unapplied cash balances at month-end.
recommended_advisory_angle: Acknowledge their General ERP / Accounting friction regarding Unapplied Cash. Share non-pitch advisory perspective on deterministic CSV/API journal matching logic.

author: Sarah Jenkins (VP Finance)
post_title: The month-end close bottleneck: Unapplied cash and bank exceptions
full_body_excerpt: Closing the books takes 8 days instead of 3 primarily because the AR team is tracking down who paid what. If the payment reference doesn't match an open invoice in Sage Intacct or NetSuite, it sits in limbo.
recommended_advisory_angle: Acknowledge their Netsuite friction regarding Unapplied Cash. Share non-pitch advisory perspective on deterministic CSV/API journal matching logic.

author: Mark Vance (Accounting Systems Manager)
post_title: Solving the BAI2 lockbox to NetSuite remittance matching problem
full_body_excerpt: Bank lockbox files give line-item check scans, but customer accounting departments rarely include invoice numbers in the check memo. We need deterministic multi-criteria matching without paying $50k/year enterprise software licenses.
recommended_advisory_angle: Acknowledge their Netsuite friction regarding Remittance. Share non-pitch advisory perspective on deterministic CSV/API journal matching logic.

author: Michael Thornton, CPA (VP Finance & Controller)
post_title: Why unapplied cash is the true enemy of financial close speed
full_body_excerpt: At our recent quarterly review, we noticed over $420,000 sitting in unapplied cash accounts across 3 entities. When ACH wires hit our Chase bank account without an invoice reference, our senior accountants have to cross-check 4 different customer portals. Closing the books in 5 days is impossible when 2 days are spent on manual AR matching.
recommended_advisory_angle: Discuss automated portal scraping and remittance matching directly against NetSuite open invoices.

author: Rachel Goldberg (Director of Accounting Operations)
post_title: The reality of lockbox banking: PDF scans and missing remittance advice
full_body_excerpt: Banks charge thousands of dollars for lockbox services, but what do they deliver? Low-resolution TIFF or PDF check images where customer remittance details are cut off. Then our team spends 15 hours a week manually re-keying invoice numbers into our ERP. There has to be a better way for mid-market companies.
recommended_advisory_angle: Share how modern OCR and AI-assisted check extraction reconciles lockbox batches into ERP journals.

author: Brian O'Connor (Chief Financial Officer @ Apex Logistics)
post_title: Evaluating AR Automation: HighRadius vs BlackLine vs Native ERP Tools
full_body_excerpt: As a $60M transportation and logistics firm, our AR team processes 2,500 customer remittances a month. HighRadius and BlackLine are built for $500M+ Fortune 500 companies with dedicated IT teams. For mid-market NetSuite users, the market has a massive gap for lightweight, high-accuracy cash application.
recommended_advisory_angle: Direct founder-to-CFO alignment on building specifically for the $20M-$100M mid-market NetSuite tier.

author: Elena Rostova (Accounting Systems Manager)
post_title: Handling many-to-many payments in NetSuite: An ongoing struggle
full_body_excerpt: When a parent company pays for 8 subsidiaries with one wire, and takes a 1.5% prompt-pay discount across 14 invoices, standard NetSuite cash application rules cannot resolve the allocation. It creates suspense account balances that haunt the audit trail.
recommended_advisory_angle: Explain parent-subsidiary cross-entity journal matching and auto-clearing logic.

author: Jason Miller, CPA (Controller @ Greenline Manufacturing)
post_title: How unapplied cash impacts customer relationships and credit limits
full_body_excerpt: Here is what happens when cash application is delayed: A customer pays $80,000 on Tuesday, but because the cash sits unapplied in suspense until Friday, our automated credit system puts their account on credit hold on Thursday. Sales is furious, customer is insulted, all because of manual reconciliation.
recommended_advisory_angle: Highlight real-time credit limit restoration when cash application happens within minutes of bank deposit.

author: Amanda Cruz (Senior AR Specialist)
post_title: Spending 6 hours every Friday downloading remittance PDFs from customer portals
full_body_excerpt: Walmart, Target, and Amazon vendors will understand: they don't email remittance advice. You have to log into 10 different supplier portals, download CSVs or PDFs, reformat columns, and manually apply payments in QuickBooks Enterprise. It is the most mind-numbing part of accounts receivable.
recommended_advisory_angle: Discuss automated vendor portal connectors that scrape and normalize remittances into ERP.

author: Thomas Wright (VP of Finance @ BioHealth Innovations)
post_title: The audit nightmare of unapplied cash balances at year-end
full_body_excerpt: External auditors spent 3 full days auditing our unapplied cash subledger because payment references did not tie cleanly to customer IDs. If your unapplied cash exceeds 2% of total AR, auditors issue a significant deficiency letter. Automating this before Q4 close is our top priority.
recommended_advisory_angle: Position Verasett clean audit trail and automated reconciliation proof reports for Big 4 auditors.
